selected_leaf: Derive the Stage T attempt-side admission rule that links one durable pre-attempt checkpoint to one exact logical_effect_id,T,w,d and prove externally visible mutation cannot be admitted from stale, replayed, incomparable, or CAS-losing checkpoint state.

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Abstract recurring-Chat Stage T protocols with one role-local CAS-protected checkpoint object, immutable logical_effect_id and exact target tuple (T,w,d), and an external mutation path whose program flow can distinguish the immediate successful CAS-return branch from ordinary read/recovery branches. No concrete product/API capability, target idempotency primitive, or eventual liveness guarantee is claimed.

pre_attempt_checkpoint.immutability: logical_effect_id,T,w,d are frozen before admission and cannot be synthesized or rotated by recovery logic.

attempt_admission_transition: 1. Fresh-read one durable checkpoint C and validate exact logical_effect_id,T,w,d plus protocol_state=VERIFY_BEFORE_ATTEMPT and mutation_permitted=false. Missing, stale, replay-only, terminal, or incomparable checkpoint evidence is not admissible.

2. Derive C_arm from exactly C: preserve logical_effect_id,T,w,d and q_last; set protocol_state=ATTEMPT_ARMED; set mutation_permitted=true; bind admission_parent_version to C.checkpoint_version and bind attempt_witness to the exact tuple (logical_effect_id,T,w,d,admission_parent_version).

3. Persist C_arm with one role-local CAS against the exact current checkpoint blob/version. The successful CAS commit is the sole admission linearization point. No external target mutation occurs before this CAS succeeds.

4. Only the immediate control-flow branch that receives that successful CAS result may submit at most one external mutation for the exact attempt_witness. A readback/recovery path that merely observes ATTEMPT_ARMED is never an admission path and must not submit mutation.

5. If CAS loses, returns ambiguous failure, or authority becomes incomparable, submit no mutation and do not retry in-run. A later recurrence rereads durable state; it cannot reconstruct the immediate successful-CAS branch from an older checkpoint.

6. After the single permitted submission attempt, the protocol must move toward VERIFY_PENDING with mutation_permitted=false when a safe checkpoint write is available. A crash before that transition leaves ATTEMPT_ARMED as a conservative recovery state: later recurrences verify/reconcile but never re-submit solely from that durable state.

non_admission_proof.stale_checkpoint: A stale C carries an obsolete checkpoint_version/blob, so its CAS precondition cannot win against a newer durable state. Because mutation is forbidden before CAS success, stale C cannot cause an external mutation.
non_admission_proof.replayed_checkpoint: Replaying the same pre-attempt C after one admission has already committed observes a changed durable checkpoint version. The replayed CAS loses; ordinary readback of ATTEMPT_ARMED is explicitly non-admitting. Therefore replay cannot produce a second admission.
non_admission_proof.incomparable_checkpoint: If exact logical_effect_id,T,w,d, authority, or checkpoint-version ordering cannot be established, the admission predicate fails before CAS. mutation_permitted remains false and no target call is issued.
non_admission_proof.cas_losing_checkpoint: A contender that loses CAS never reaches the unique successful-CAS control-flow branch. Since target mutation is sequenced strictly after CAS success, the loser cannot submit mutation.
non_admission_proof.terminal_or_recovery_state: COMMITTED, CONFLICT, VERIFY_PENDING and read-observed ATTEMPT_ARMED have no transition into a target-call branch. Verifier consumption from the predecessor slice also never re-arms mutation.

race_argument: All contenders derived from one pre-attempt checkpoint version race on the same CAS-protected role-local state object; at most one can commit C_arm for that version.
The only target-call edge is dominated by that successful CAS result, so every CAS loser has zero target-call edges.

After a winner commits C_arm, the predecessor checkpoint is stale. Subsequent recurrences observe ATTEMPT_ARMED through readback, not through the winning CAS-return branch, and therefore cannot re-submit from the durable arm state.

This proves at-most-one admission from a checkpoint version under the stated program-flow model. It does not yet prove target-side exactly-once effect if a single admitted network submission itself is internally duplicated by the target or transport.
bounded_leaf_result.direct_architecture_contribution: The attempt side can be made checkpoint-first and CAS-linearized using only lightweight repository state transport: external mutation is unreachable until one exact pre-attempt checkpoint wins CAS, and stale/replayed/incomparable/CAS-losing states are structurally excluded from the mutation branch. This closes the predecessor slice's unresolved admission ordering at the abstract architecture level without richer-mode arbitration.
unresolved_conditions: A concrete implementation must enforce the control-flow invariant that only the immediate successful-CAS branch can invoke the target mutation and that recovery/readback of ATTEMPT_ARMED cannot invoke it.

A concrete target/transport must be assessed for duplication inside a single admitted submission; this slice proves admission at-most-once from checkpoint state, not target-side exactly-once application.

A later bounded leaf must connect the post-submission crash window to VERIFY_PENDING and the q_last verifier-consumption gate, classifying response-loss and target duplication without permitting a second mutation call.
